correctness.rationale: Stationary two-state Markov moments give \(m=\pi d\), \(z=(d-m)r\) and \(S=3m^2+mz(2+r)\). Their unique algebraic inverse holds for all admissible \(r\ne0\) because \(d-m>0\) and the square-root factor \(d(1-v)>0\). When \(r=0\), the entire ordered observation process is iid Bernoulli with parameter \(m\) and is nonidentifiable; for two visits a continuous family keeps \(m\) and the sole pair probability fixed. The Jacobian is \(-2d^5\pi^2(1-\pi)[\pi+(1-\pi)r]r^2\), proving exactly the same nonsingular locus. An exact-rational checker ran successfully for 687 admissible nonzero-memory triples and three zero-memory cases. Computations do not constitute the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The sharp globally invertible three-visit unlabelled count law for a hidden Markov availability chain with a separate unknown imperfect detector is not implied by the inspected neighboring results on ordered histories, directly observed Markov-binomial counts, or independently repeated binomial N-mixtures. Six targeted published-record queries, primary literature inspections, and comparisons with accessible related findings did not reveal equivalent or stronger coverage. Search nonappearance is not a proof of novelty; priority and possible broader inverse-thinning theorems remain explicit residual risks.
residual_risks: A more general theorem on identifiability of thinned Markov-binomial totals might directly imply the formulas even if not indexed by the targeted search terms.
The source inspections concentrated on the relevant full-text model and theorem sections; an uninspected appendix or older monograph may contain an equivalent inversion.
Assumptions such as known persistent site occupancy and homogeneous detection substantially delimit the scientific reach.

value.rationale: Ecological survey programs often record detection totals while temporary unavailability and sensor misses confound one another. A sharp minimal visit number for aggregate counts, closed-form recovery of transition and detection parameters and a complete boundary of unavoidable nonidentifiability are structural and nonroutine even within the intentionally idealized known-occupied model. The quadratic Jacobian collapse indicates the expected difficulty near independence; no finite-sample precision or broader ecological theorem is claimed.
